issues.issue: The disclaimer that use of the Materials may infringe third-party rights sits alongside section 1's acknowledgment of St. Jude's own patents and section 5's ownership claim, but no operative provision allocates infringement risk; the tension is mild.

"Any and all claims, demands or legal causes of action of any nature whatsoever ... arising out of or related to Recipient's acceptance, use and disposal of the Materials" is a general catch-all closed by a specific illustration (personal injury or death), leaving the reach of the general words uncertain — in particular whether claims by St. Jude itself, or claims arising from St. Jude's own conduct, are covered.

The written amount and the numeral conflict: "Three Million ($1,000,000) dollars aggregate" pairs the word "Three Million" with a one-million figure, so the required aggregate limit is uncertain on the face of the clause. "Occurrence basis, or claims made including tail coverage" also leaves the choice of form to the Recipient without any duration for the tail.

"Breaches any term and fails to cure such breach within thirty (30) days after written notice" does not say whether the notice must specify the breach or how an incurable breach is treated, so whether a purported termination was effective can turn on the words.

The obligation to cease all use and return all Materials and progeny sits uneasily with section 3, which permits use in quantities sufficient to complete a Phase I clinical trial, and with the survival sentence of section 10; what happens to material already incorporated into a vector or administered to patients is not addressed.

The survival list reads "Sections 5, 5 and 7," naming the same number twice; because the letter itself contains two paragraphs numbered 5 and no paragraph 6, which provisions survive termination cannot be determined from the text. This is a mechanical numbering error that changes what the clause does.

It cannot be reconciled with the body of the MTA, which duplicates the number 5 (ownership/publication and warranty disclaimer) and skips 6 entirely, so the cross-reference has no coherent referent in the instrument as a whole.

The letter contemplates signature by Dr. June and an authorized official of his institution, while the signature block also carries a University of Pennsylvania Office of Research Services signatory; whether the Agreement is formed absent one of those signatures is a whole-instrument question.
